brief: Lane rb2: implement stages R0-R2 of hybrid continuous batching for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (NVFP4) on CUDA (DGX Spark GB10): row-exact (G-B) kernels, plan/memory/engine plumbing, CUDA bring-up with batched logits bitwise equal to solo (G-C), cap 16, MTP and prefix store stay at batch 1. User approval 06:41 EDT: 'start R0-R2 recurrent batching, cap 16 on CUDA'.
hypothesis: The 35B serves one sequence at a time because the batched engine refused recurrent state and CUDA registered no row-exact multi-row kernels. The CUDA decode GEMVs are warp-per-row with a fixed K partition, so row-exact multi-row twins are cheap; batching the dense projections and the MoE (row, expert) pairs, with GDN and attention per row, should lift 4-stream aggregate decode from 75.2 toward 140 tok/s with every row bitwise the solo step.

summary: R0-R2 done and gated; speed target missed. Row-exact CUDA GEMV and MoE decode kernels (M up to 16) registered rows_exact, a kernel-pick plan check with a proven-fusion table, per-backend cap 16, recurrent state in the memory plan, and a CUDA bring-up of hybrid batching. Every decode row is bitwise the solo step (4290 row-steps each on the 35B and Qwen3-8B), the batched engine equals LocalEngine, and plan show + 256 ids are unchanged with batching off. 35B aggregate decode in the composer cell, same build with batching off as 'before': 123.3 at 4 streams (74.1; the 10-22 baseline was 75.2; target about 140) and 166.6 at 16 (74.2); 1 stream unchanged (73.4). Verdict win against the baseline (x1.63 at 4, x2.21 at 16, nothing lost at 1) but the lane's stated 4-stream target is not met; at 4 streams the step already runs at model-loop speed (25.7 vs 25.4 ms) and the burst is 0.9 s of serialized prefill plus 127 steps, so 140 needs a step about 15% cheaper or prefill overlapped with decode; per-row GDN and attention launches (25% of a B=4 step, 42% at B=16) and the eager batched step are the lever at 16 streams. Busy-chunk follow-up: busy chunk 1024 failed the KL gate (mean 21-way KL 7.87e-3 vs 3.161e-3 floor), so the default busy chunk is now the solo chunk (2048): whole requests are token-identical to LocalEngine on 2.6k-16k prompts, with no speed cost on the 1k workload; 1024 stays opt-in.
lessons: Raising the busy prefill chunk from 256 to 1024 for the MoE hybrid was worth +18% at 4 streams and +30% at 16 (104 to 123, 128 to 167): an MoE prefill chunk reads nearly all experts at any size, so stalls dominate a short-output concurrent benchmark.
check_batch_ops must compare kernel picks, not op multisets: the CUDA MoE switches kernel under one Op between m <= 1 and m >= 2, which the multiset rule cannot see.

On the Spark the CUDA free figure after loading a 20 GB model is MemFree, not MemAvailable: page cache from other models' files left 1.9 GB for KV and recurrent state of a 16-slot engine; evict other files' cache (dd iflag=nocache count=0) before benchmarks, or the plan caps the context.

At 4 streams the serve burst (4.17 s) is 0.90 s of serialized 1k-token prefill plus 127 steps of 25.7 ms, equal to the model-loop step (25.4 ms): the gap to 140 is prefill time and the step, not engine overhead. At 16 streams 3.93 s of prefill plus 127 steps of 65.9 ms (model loop 65.3).

Prefill chunk size is part of the numerics on this engine: busy-chunk 1024 vs solo 2048 prefill gives 2.5x the vLLM run-to-run KL floor on the 35B, and 256 is no better; a busy chunk equal to the solo chunk is bitwise by construction.
